prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1427; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in a sedan and turning left at an intersection in Houston, Texas, when the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, who was proceeding straight through on the opposite approach. Driver 1 was the only occupant other than the Passenger, who was seated beside them in the front. Driver 1 reported neck and back pain at the scene and was transported for evaluation. The force of the impact is consistent with the injuries described. The damage to the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle matches the direction and severity of the collision. Driver 2 gave a statement that agrees with Driver 1's account of how the crash occurred. Two independent witnesses on the sidewalk confirmed the sequence of events and identified both the Driver 1 and the Passenger as occupants of the vehicle at the time. Scene photographs were taken and are on file. Driver 1 reported no prior damage to the vehicle, and none was observed. Records indicate that Driver 1 resides in the same household as the named policyholder and is listed as a covered household member.
